Page 03 · 01 Who We Are
01 · Who We Are
01

Senior marketing
that moves with you.

Digital Connex Agency+ is a senior-led marketing partner for ambitious small and mid-sized businesses. We work on subscription, replace the need for a traditional in-house team, and move at the pace of the people we serve.

What we do

Lean Marketing Solutions.

Three tiered retainers — Lite, Growth, Pro — that flex with client stage. Strategy, creative, content, paid, analytics, PR. Delivered by a small senior team, not a junior pool.

Who we're for

Founders with momentum.

Businesses post product-market fit, pre-scale. Every dollar needs to work harder than it would at a bigger shop.

What we believe

Fewer hands, deeper work.

Most agencies overstaff junior and underinvest senior. We do the opposite. Consistent context, less translation loss between strategy and execution.

Our north star

Compounding, not campaigns.

We don't chase one-off wins. We build marketing systems that compound — owned content, owned audience, owned data, owned brand.

"This brand is how we show up before we open our mouths. Every logo placement, every email sign-off, every pitch deck should say: these people know what they're doing, and they care about the details."
Page 04 · 02 Logo System
02 · Logo System
02

The mark.

A wordmark with a geometric parallelogram behind connex, angled right. Five variants — and one rule that ties them together: the parallelogram's colour is the page's colour.

Primary — Gradient

Feature moments · covers, hero, launch 1Primary_Gradient.png

Navy — on cream

Default · standard pages 3Navy_Text.png

Navy — inverted

Navy pages · #16275A bg 2Navy_Inverted.png

Black — on cream

Monochrome · editorial 5Black_Text.png

Black — inverted

Black pages · #292929 bg 4Black_Inverted.png
The rule. Parallelogram fill equals page background. Navy parallelogram → navy page. Black parallelogram → black page. The shape dissolves into the bg; only the cream cut-out text reads. This is the signature move of the system.
Page 05 · 03 Logo Usage
03 · Logo Usage
03

Protect the mark.

The logo only works if it's used consistently. A few simple rules keep it sharp.

Do

  • Use the correct variant for the background
  • Pair navy-inverted on navy pages; black-inverted on black pages
  • Maintain clear-space buffer on every side
  • Use transparent PNGs provided — never re-export with a white box
  • Scale proportionally from a corner
  • Place on clean, high-contrast backgrounds

Don't

  • Mix variants — navy wordmark on a black bg, etc.
  • Change the colours — ever
  • Rotate, skew, or flip the logo
  • Place on busy photography without contrast treatment
  • Add effects — drop shadows, outlines, glows, bevels
  • Recreate the logo in a different typeface
  • Crop the parallelogram container
Co-branding. When placing the DC logo next to a client or partner logo, use a vertical rule (1pt, Jet Black at 20% opacity) separating them, with equal clear space on both sides. Never merge marks.

Secondary — DC monogram

For tight contexts where the wordmark won't fit — favicons, avatars, watermarks. Six variants follow the same colour-on-bg rule as the primary.

Signature
Navy → Sky
135° gradient
Navy to Sky Blue
  • Royalty Navy — primary brand colour. Headlines, dark page backgrounds, primary CTA fills.
  • Sky Blue — accent. Eyebrow labels, section numbers, dividers, hyperlinks. Never large solid fills.
  • Jet Black — body copy. Softer than true black (#000), reduces eye strain.
  • Creamy White — default page background. Warmer than pure white, matches print feel.
  • Anti-White — pullquotes, cards on cream, subtle surface contrast. The only "grey" we use.
  • Gradient — covers, hero sections, feature moments. Never for body content.
Page 07 · 05 Codec Pro
05 · Codec Pro
05

Codec Pro.
The primary voice.

Heavy headlines set the tone. Regular body earns the trust. Every text element sits on the Fibonacci scale — no in-between sizes, no drift.

Display · Codec Pro Heavy 900
Headlines.
55pt · line-height 1.13 · letter-spacing -0.055em
H2 · Codec Pro Heavy 900
Section openers go here.
34pt · line-height 1.13 · letter-spacing -0.055em
H3 · Codec Pro Heavy 900
Lead paragraph voice.
21pt · line-height 1.13 · letter-spacing -0.055em
Sub-head · Codec Pro Bold 700
Introduces a block of content.
13pt · line-height 1.2 · letter-spacing -0.034em
Body · Codec Pro Regular 400
Body copy is where the thinking lives. It carries the weight of the argument, the nuance of the strategy, the specifics of the work. Keep lines tight, letter-spacing negative, line-height comfortable.
13pt · line-height 1.34 · letter-spacing -0.021em
Small · Codec Pro Regular 400
Captions, footnotes, fine print, labels — all at 8pt. Used sparingly, never for reading content.
8pt · line-height 1.34 · letter-spacing -0.021em
Fallback stack. If Codec Pro is unavailable, fall back to Inter Display for headlines and Inter for body. Both are free via Google Fonts and share Codec Pro's geometric character closely.
Page 08 · 06 Bauer Bodoni
06 · Bauer Bodoni
06

Bauer Bodoni.
The editorial counterpoint.

A classic high-contrast serif used for moments of editorial refinement. Display use only. Never body. Never competing with Codec Pro.

Editorial Display · Bauer Bodoni Italic
Section openers.
55pt · line-height 1.0 · italic · letter-spacing -0.034em
Pull Quote · Bauer Bodoni Italic
"The typography carries the tone before a single word is read."
21pt · line-height 1.34 · italic
Feature Numeral · Bauer Bodoni
01.
89pt · case study openers, section flourishes, chapter numerals

Use Bauer Bodoni for

  • Editorial section openers in case studies
  • Pull quotes and emphasis callouts (italic)
  • Large feature numerals (chapters, steps)
  • Rare hero display moments

Never for

  • Body copy — ever. Codec Pro owns running text.
  • UI elements — buttons, form labels, small text
  • Logo treatments or brand lockups
  • Every page in a row — it's a spice, not a staple
Rule of thumb. If you're using Bauer Bodoni more than once per document spread, you're probably overusing it. Elegant minimalism means restraint — one editorial moment per page, maximum. Fallbacks: Noto Serif Display (free) or Didot.
Page 09 · 07 Spacing & Grid
07 · Spacing & Grid
07

Fibonacci.
Not arbitrary.

Every value in the system comes from the Fibonacci sequence — spacing, font sizes, border radii, even letter-spacing and line-height as ratios. It creates a rhythm the eye trusts, even when it can't name why.

The sequence we use

8
13
21
34
55
89

All values in pixels. Each step is the sum of the previous two (8+13=21, 13+21=34, 21+34=55, 34+55=89). Under 8 we use 3 and 5 for very fine detail.

Font sizes

8 · 13 · 21 · 34 · 55 · 89pt

Small text 8pt. Main body 13pt. Sub-heads 21pt. Section headers 34pt. Display 55pt. Editorial hero 89pt. No in-between sizes.

Spacing

3 · 5 · 8 · 13 · 21 · 34 · 55 · 89px

Micro (3, 5) for fine detail. Tight (8, 13) inside components. Medium (21, 34) between blocks. Large (55, 89) between sections.

Line-height

1.13 · 1.34

1.13 for headings (tight, Fibonacci-derived 13). 1.34 for body (comfortable for reading, Fibonacci-derived 34).

Letter-spacing

-0.021 · -0.034 · -0.055em

Body at -0.021em. Sub-heads at -0.034em. Display at -0.055em. The negative tracking is what gives the type its character.

Layout grid — 12 columns

12-column grid with 21px gutters. Most content uses 6-wide or 12-wide spans.

Page 10 · 08 Voice & Tone
08 · Voice & Tone
08

Warm. Direct.
Never precious.

Our voice is warm, approachable, and collaborative — the way a trusted senior friend would explain something complex over coffee. Never corporate, never jargon-heavy, never performatively clever.

Warm

Human, not transactional.

We remember that every email lands on a real person's desk. Use contractions. First names. Light warmth even in formal comms.

Approachable

Plain words, always.

Never gate-keep with jargon. If we use a technical term, we define it. Accessibility over polish.

Collaborative

"We" more than "I".

Frame things as something we're figuring out together, not a verdict being handed down. Curiosity over certainty.

Direct, when it matters

Warmth never costs clarity.

If something isn't working, say so — kindly, specifically, with a way forward. Never hedge into mush.

Two voice modes

The warm baseline applies to 90% of what we write — client emails, onboarding, social, the blog. A second mode — confident/strategic — is reserved for documents where the client is hiring us for our POV: pitch proposals, strategy docs, board-level reports. Still warm, but more definitive. Less "we think, maybe", more "here's what we'd do, and why".

The test. Read anything you write out loud. If it sounds like a person you'd want to work with, it's on-brand. If it sounds like a press release, rewrite it.
Page 11 · 09 Voice in Practice
09 · Voice in Practice
09

Say this.
Not that.

Concrete examples. The patterns that come up most often, and the corrections that keep us on-brand.

Say this

Happy to jump on a call this week if it's useful.
We've had a look — here's what we'd do first.
Quick update: the campaign's tracking ahead of plan.
A few thoughts before we lock this in.
Our gut says option B. Here's why.
That didn't land the way we hoped — here's what we'll change.

Not that

Please advise at your earliest convenience regarding a synchronous touchpoint.
Per our analysis, the following recommendations have been formulated.
I'm pleased to inform you that KPIs are exceeding benchmarks.
Prior to finalising, please find below some key considerations.
Our data-driven recommendation is option B.
Unfortunately, the campaign underperformed against projected KPIs.

Words we don't use

  • Leverage (as a verb). Use use.
  • Synergy, alignment, ecosystem, touchpoint, bandwidth. Agency jargon.
  • Unlock, unleash, transform, disrupt, revolutionise. Reserve for when they're literally true.
  • At the end of the day / at this point in time / going forward. Fillers. Delete.
Page 12 · 10 Imagery
10 · Imagery & Photography
10

Real people,
real work.

Our imagery should feel like a candid glimpse into actual work — clients, projects, and the studio — not glossy stock. Always prefer real over staged.

Subject matter

Where the work happens.

Behind-the-scenes moments from shoots, laptop-open meetings, strategy sessions, studio setups. Clients where we have permission. Our own team in flow.

Lighting & mood

Warm, natural, un-retouched.

Daylight where possible. Warm tungsten in studio. Shadows are welcome — they add depth. Avoid hard flash, heavy retouching, or HDR processing.

Colour treatment

Warm neutral, pulled slightly cool.

Baseline tone leans slightly cool and matte. Never oversaturated. Blacks lifted slightly to sit in the Creamy White world. Reference: Apple's product photography.

Composition

Breathing room, off-centre subjects.

Strong negative space. Rule of thirds. Landscape orientation preferred for hero images. Wide shots over close-ups when setting scene.

Never

  • Stock photography — no "diverse team high-fiving around a laptop", ever
  • Over-retouched skin, perfect lighting, studio-model feel
  • Cliché business imagery — handshakes, arrow graphics, "climbing ladders"
  • AI-generated people (uncanny valley kills trust instantly)
Page 13 · 11 Motion
11 · Motion & Video
11

Considered,
not kinetic.

Motion should feel purposeful — a slow reveal, a confident transition, a deliberate emphasis. Avoid anything that feels "look what I can do" — whip pans, aggressive zooms, stacked transitions, beat-sync overload.

Timing

Slow over fast.

Default transitions 400–600ms. Cuts on beats are fine; cuts every beat is not. Let moments breathe.

Camera work

Locked off or slow dolly.

Tripod or gimbal. Never handheld shake. Slow push-ins on interview subjects. Locked wide for establishing shots.

Type in motion

Subtle, small, late.

Titles fade in 200ms after the cut lands. No spinning text, no kinetic typography templates. Codec Pro Heavy stays Codec Pro Heavy.

Colour grade

Matches photography.

Same warm-neutral-pulled-cool grade as our stills. Slightly lifted blacks, desaturated greens, protected skin tones.

Sound

  • Music. Ambient, textured, instrumental. Nothing lyrical in client-facing work.
  • Voice. Real people, real audio. Lavalier mics or boom. Never AI voiceover on client work.
  • Silence. Let it sit. A two-second hold does more work than a soundtrack.
Page 14 · 12 Documents
12 · Documents & Templates
12

Every document,
the same backbone.

Every DC document uses the same structural rhythm — cover, header, section number, headline, divider, lead, body, close. Consistency across formats is what makes the brand feel like a brand.

Template family

  • Pitch/Proposal. For new leads. Strategic voice. Cover → Summary → Understanding → Challenge → Strategy → Scope → Investment → Timeline → Close.
  • Onboarding Brief. For signed clients. Warm voice. Cover → Welcome → Team → How We Work → Kickoff → Discovery → 30/60/90 → Access → Expectations → Close.
  • Brand Guidelines. Monochrome editorial. Creamy White + Jet Black only. Colour appears as content, not chrome.
  • Monthly Report. Short, data-led. Summary → Wins → Numbers → What we're testing → Next month.
  • Case Study. Challenge → Approach → Work → Result → Quote. One page per section.

Page anatomy

  • Page header. Mini logo left, section tag top-right (-0.034em letter-spacing).
  • Section number. Large serif numeral at 8% opacity, behind the headline.
  • H2 headline. 34pt Codec Pro Heavy, line-break for rhythm.
  • Divider. 55px × 2px Jet Black rule.
  • Lead paragraph. 13pt. Sets up what's on the page.
  • Body. 13pt. Two-column blocks or prose.
File naming. DC_[DocType]_[Client]_[Version]_[YYYYMMDD].pdf. Example: DC_Proposal_FairBuild_v2_20260417.pdf
Page 15 · 13 Maintenance
13 · Maintenance
13

A brand is
a living thing.

These guidelines are v1.0. They'll evolve — but only deliberately, and always documented. If something's unclear or missing, raise it. If it's working, leave it alone.

Review cadence

  • Quarterly check-in. Is anything in here wrong, outdated, or unclear in practice?
  • Annual refresh. Full review. Deprecate what isn't working. Document what is.
  • Ad-hoc updates. A new template, a new colour, a new voice principle? Add it — don't let the doc drift from reality.

Asset locations

  • Logo files (all variants). Shared drive: /Brand/Logos/ — transparent PNG + SVG + source.
  • Codec Pro font files. Licensed primary typeface, seats managed by Humzeh.
  • Bauer Bodoni font files. Secondary display typeface, display-only use.
  • Document templates. Pitch & Onboarding templates, editable source.
  • Collateral templates. Canva team library, linked from brand hub.
